# Ammunition Types
Different ammunition types are designed for different targets. Their construction affects how well they perform against armor and may provide additional effects.
## Soft Point
Soft Point is a general-purpose ammunition type. It is a reliable choice when no specialized ammunition is available, but is less effective against armored targets.
## Hollow Point
Hollow Point ammunition is designed to maximize damage against unarmored threats. It performs poorly against armor and should generally be avoided when engaging protected targets.
## Full Metal Jacket
Full Metal Jacket is a versatile ammunition type suited for both armored and crowded threats. Its improved armor performance makes it a dependable choice when dealing with protected targets.
FMJ ammunition also has the property of piercing through targets, allowing a single shot to potentially strike multiple enemies.
## Armor Piercing
Armor Piercing ammunition is intended for heavily armored threats. It is particularly effective against heavily protected personnel and armored machines where conventional ammunition may struggle.
## Shotgun Ammunition
### Buckshot
Buckshot fires multiple projectiles at once, making it effective against unarmored targets. Its individual pellets are less effective against armor.
### Slug
Slug ammunition fires a single large projectile. Unlike buckshot, it is highly effective against armored targets and is a strong choice when concentrated damage and armor penetration are required.
## Specialty Ammunition
Some ammunition types do not have a special interaction with armor but instead provide unique effects.
- [color=cyan]Incendiary:[/color] Produces additional heat and can ignite targets. - [color=cyan]Rubber:[/color] Designed for non-lethal applications. - [color=cyan]Practice:[/color] Low-damage training ammunition. - [color=cyan]Uranium:[/color] Inflicts additional radiation damage.
